subject: dragonling
pitch: A baby dragon the size of a house cat, sitting proudly beside the broken shell of its speckled egg. Teal scales fading to a buttery belly, stubby horns, a row of soft orange spines down its back, oversized wings it can't fly with yet, with translucent amber skin between the fingers, and a chubby tail ending in a little spade. Big amber eyes, a toothy grin and a wisp of smoke curling from one nostril.
reasoning:
I'm uncertain about the exact SDK signatures, so I should stick to a safer subset of functions like createBuilder, joint, chain, part, sweep, and extrude, inferring their parameters carefully from the reference material rather than guessing.

Given the risk of getting part/rod/spike signatures wrong, I'm considering a fallback approach: use the joint API for the skeleton structure, but construct meshes directly with THREE.js objects attached to the joints to avoid relying on uncertain SDK calls.

I'll go with adding the root joint to b.root and placing meshes at world coordinates, assuming identity transform there. I'm sketching a small mesh helper function with cached materials, then planning the dragon's sitting pose—torso, pelvis, chest, and head positions—with the egg placed beside it at a slightly offset coordinate.

Now I'm working out the haunches, forward hind feet, and front arm capsules, then plotting the tail as a curling series of shrinking spheres sampled along a Catmull-Rom curve, ending in a spade shape, curving away from the egg's side. I'm also starting to position small folded wings near the shoulders.

Writing wing membrane geometry...

Adding more facial details next: a separate jaw with teeth, amber eyes with pupils, backward-angled horns, and smoking nostrils, plus cream belly plates on the torso and the start of an egg shape built from scaled spheres.

For the egg, I'm shaping the broken bottom shell with a jagged cone rim, speckled brown spots, a lighter double-sided inner surface, and a few scattered shell fragments nearby, possibly with a small straw-colored nest base beneath it.

Working out the shell geometry math to position the speckles correctly along the bottom ellipsoid curve without sinking them below the visible rim.

I'm now planning the skeleton joint hierarchy, setting up hips, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, tail segments, shoulders, and wings using a helper function to define each joint's position and parent.

Now I'm picking out the color palette (teals, belly amber, orange, wing membrane) and building geometry helper functions for ellipsoids, rods, and cones to construct the body parts, starting with the torso's shape and tilt.

Positioning the chest, belly, neck, and throat shapes...

Now shaping the head and snout with a rounded ellipsoid tip, adding a lower jaw, dark mouth interior, and placing teeth cones along both jaws.

I'll place the dark mouth ellipse with upper teeth visible and keep lower teeth minimal since they'd mostly hide inside the snout. For the eyes, I'm placing big amber spheres with black pupils offset toward the viewing direction, tiny white highlights, and a teal brow ridge above each, then moving on to the nostrils.

Now I'm positioning dark nostril holes and adding a small spiral of smoke puffs curling up from the left nostril with decreasing opacity per segment. I'm adding cream-colored horn cones tapering up and back, skipping cheek frills and ear fins for simplicity, and starting the arm geometry from shoulder to elbow.

Continuing the limbs, I'm defining teal arm segments ending in cream claw-tipped hands, haunch and foot ellipsoids with small toe cones, and finally building the tail as a Catmull-Rom spline of tapering spheres curving from the body out to a thin tip.

For the tail's flat spade-shaped end, I'm sketching a diamond outline and extruding it slightly, then orienting it to lie flat along the tail's tangent direction.

Working out rotation matrices...

Now I'm positioning the tail end and thinking about raising it to match the spade height, then moving on to lay out dorsal spine points along a curve from the neck down through the torso.

Checking that the dorsal spine points actually sit on the torso surface -- recalculating z-depth at each y-level against the ellipsoid's radii to make sure the spines don't float inside or outside the body, adjusting the cone sizes to shrink gradually with orange coloring and slightly sunken bases.

Now I'm working out the wing geometry: shoulder, elbow, and three fingertip points positioned relative to the side (left/right), plus a body anchor point to form the membrane. I'm fanning triangles from the elbow point across the fingertips down to the anchor and shoulder to create the webbed wing shape, keeping the wings oversized and extended outward in a resting, slightly lifted pose.

I'm setting the membrane material to be translucent amber (double-sided, low opacity, no depth write), the finger rods thin teal-dark cylinders, thicker arm bones, and a small cream claw cone at the wrist. I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy—shoulder parented to chest, then wrist, then finger joints—for the left wing on the positive X side, and positioning the feet, egg, and tail to avoid overlap on the sitting pose.

Now I'm placing the egg roughly centered beside the dragon so the overall silhouette (tail extending negative X through the wing's positive X reach) stays balanced, considering a small global offset to better center the composition. I'm also sketching broken eggshell fragments as flattened sphere caps scaled down in height, positioned near the egg with slight rotation so they look like scattered shards.

Writing shell and speckle code...

I'm skipping the interior goo detail and instead considering adding a small tan torus as a nest ring around the egg, checking it won't collide with the dragon's hand given their positions, and sizing the tube thickness accordingly.

Now I'm planning helper functions for building the mesh: a rod function that creates a cylinder oriented between two points, and a cone function for tapered shapes, all added to the root with flat shading. I'm also working through how to define joints with parent relationships, weighing whether to pass the parent as a joint object or by name, aware there's some risk of errors if the API expects something different.
